summary.short: Bill PL 2768/2022 would let Anatel regulate digital platforms serving the Brazilian public. Platforms with R$70 million or more in annual operating revenue would be designated as holding essential access-control power and face transparency, non-discrimination, data-use and access duties, plus competition-law limits and a fee-funded oversight fund. Effective on publication.
summary.long: Bill PL 2768/2022 would regulate the organisation, operation and oversight of digital platforms offering services to the Brazilian public, assigning Anatel that role. Anatel would gain powers to issue rules, interpret the law administratively, settle conflicts between operators and professional users, repress user-rights infringements and handle competition matters outside CADE's remit. Covered platform modalities include search, social networks, intermediation, operating systems and cloud computing. Operators with annual Brazilian operating revenue of R$ 70 million or more would be deemed to hold essential access-control power and bear duties on transparency, non-discriminatory treatment, appropriate use of collected data and not refusing platform access to professional users; Anatel may impose separation, data-portability and interoperability measures. Concentrations and certain contract practices are subject to competition control. A Digital Platform Oversight Fund (FisDigi) would be created, financed by an annual fee on essential-access-control operators and other sources. Sanctions include warnings, fines up to 2% of Brazilian group revenue, obligations to do or not do, temporary suspension and prohibition of activities; foreign firms' Brazilian branches are jointly liable for fines. Effective on publication.

enforcement.triggered_by: Infringements of the norms set out in this Law, applied alone or cumulatively with other sanctions
enforcement.max_penalty_text: multa de até 2% (dois por cento) do faturamento do grupo econômico no Brasil no seu último exercício, excluídos os tributos
enforcement.penalty_formula: Up to 2% of the economic group's gross revenue in Brazil in the last fiscal year, excluding taxes; the economic condition of the infringer and proportionality between gravity of the breach and intensity of the sanction are considered (Art. 16 II). Under Art. 16 §3 the fine may be applied to revenue for the whole period of the conduct, capped at 1% of that value. Under Art. 16 §1, a foreign company is jointly liable for the fine with its Brazilian branch, subsidiary, office or establishment.
